D022-D023_h001.question: It's been a tough few months, doc. I feel like I'm losing control. At least once a week, usually after a long shift, I just eat myself sick. I'll get home, and before I know it, I’ve gone through a whole pizza, a tub of ice cream, and god knows what else, all in one sitting. It's way more than anyone should eat, and I feel so guilty afterward, so disgusted with myself. The next day, sometimes, in a panic, I’ll take a bunch of laxatives, thinking it’ll just undo everything. But it’s not a regular thing, just when I feel particularly awful about what I’ve done. When I look in the mirror, all I see is this huge, fat guy, like I’m twice the size I actually am. My gut feels enormous, even though I know it can’t be as bad as I see it.

D022-D023_h002.question:
"It’s tough to talk about, Doc. I’ve been a firefighter for five years, and it's a demanding job; I always try to be at my best. But lately, I’ve felt like I'm losing control. For the past four months or so, I’ve been having these episodes—usually after a stressful shift or a disagreement with my wife. I'll just eat massive amounts of food, way more than anyone reasonably should, usually in secret. I’m talking about finishing an entire pizza, then moving onto a box of donuts, all in one sitting.

Afterward, the guilt and shame just eat me alive. I feel so disgusted with myself that I’ve tried to make myself throw up sometimes to get rid of it all. It’s not something I do every time, maybe only once or twice a month, but each time I do, I swear it’ll be the last. I know it’s not normal. My self-worth is completely tied to my weight and how I look; if I’m not lean and strong, I feel like a failure, not just as a firefighter, but as a person, a husband. This isn't me, and I need to figure out how to stop."
D022-D023_h002.options:
A. Anorexia Nervosa
    B. Bulimia Nervosa
    C. Binge-Eating Disorder
    D. Acute Stress Disorder
